text: Most demos of agents verifying their own work only ever show the happy path. I wanted to see mine actually fail first, diagnose itself, and fix itself, live, with nothing scripted in advance.

This is Q A Copilot, built for the Kane C L I Online Hackathon. You give it a deployed U R L and describe a flow in plain English. It runs that flow through Kane C L I, in a real browser, against the real site. When Kane fails the flow, the agent reads Kane's own evidence, writes a bug report, rewrites the objective, and tries again automatically. That loop is the whole point of this build.

I'm pointing it at a public Q A practice site run by Sauce Labs, not one of my own projects, so there's nothing staged about what happens next. The objective I'm giving it makes a claim that is actually false: that a page which returns a real 500 status code loads successfully with no error.
Kane C L I is now driving an actual Chrome browser against that live page. This isn't a mock or a recorded trace, it's a real run, right now, burning real Kane credits.

And there it is: attempt one, failed. Kane correctly caught that the page really did return its 500 error, which means my objective's claim was wrong. Look at the bug report the agent wrote. It didn't just say fail, it diagnosed exactly why: the objective expected an error free page, but a 500 status code page is supposed to show an error. That's a sharp, specific diagnosis, not a generic failure message.

Now watch what the agent does with that. It takes Kane's own evidence, and rewrites the objective to match reality: instead of asserting there's no error, it now expects the 500 error message to actually be there. It's re running Kane right now with that corrected objective.
Same agent, same tool, no human in the loop, closing the gap it just found in itself.

Attempt two: passed. The corrected objective holds up, because now it actually matches what the page does. That's the closed loop: Kane's result fed back into the agent, and the agent's correction fed back into Kane.

Under the hood this is a small Express server that shells out to kane dash c l i run in agent mode, parses its own structured run end event, and only calls an L L M when there's an actual failure to diagnose. Every attempt is kept, so you can see the full back and forth, not just a final badge. It's also deployed publicly with bring your own key support, so anyone, including judges, can run it with their own TestMu A I account instead of mine.
Repo link and the live U R L are below. Built end to end with Claude Code. Thanks for watching.
